result.title: Words to World: Benchmarking LLMs in Interactive Physical Environments
result.summary: Words are increasingly becoming an interface for action: large language models (LLMs) can now invoke tools, operate devices, and make decisions that affect the physical world. However, current benchmarks largely evaluate LLMs through static text responses, offline tool calls, or simulated tasks, leaving open the question of how well they can act in real physical environments. We present a benchmark for measuring LLMs in closed-loop physical interaction, where models control a harness system connected to real-world components including robotic arms, cameras, and sensors. In each task, the model must issue instructions, receive physical feedback from the environment, interpret the resulting state, and adapt its next action accordingly. This setting evaluates capabilities beyond language understanding, including grounded perception, action planning, tool selection, spatial reasoning, feedback-driven correction, and robustness to execution uncertainty. Through experiments with representative LLMs, we characterize their ability to translate linguistic reasoning into physical actions and identify common failure modes such as hallucinated state changes, poor recovery from unexpected outcomes, and unstable long-horizon plans. Our benchmark aims to provide a systematic foundation for evaluating LLMs as interactive agents that connect words, tools, and the physical world.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一个闭环物理交互基准，让 LLM 控制连接机械臂、相机与传感器的装置，按指令获取环境物理反馈、解读状态并调整下一步动作，并用代表性模型刻画其失败模式（如幻觉状态变化、异常恢复差、长程计划不稳定）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「行动—感知反馈—状态解读—修正」的闭环设定与执行不确定性，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据获取、内部状态更新与停止决策的收益成本问题相关，可供核查；但该工作面向具身智能体，不直接研究 latent 视觉推理。
